client-go/cache: encode *unstructured.Unstructured at rest as CBOR in ThreadSafeStore

Problem
-------
ThreadSafeStore (the backing store for every informer cache) holds all
objects as fully-deserialized Go values in map[string]interface{}.  A
*unstructured.Unstructured is a deeply-nested map[string]interface{} tree
where every field — strings, numbers, nested maps — is a separately-boxed,
individually GC-tracked heap allocation.  For controllers managing thousands
of unstructured resources this dominates process memory.

Real-world impact (argoproj/argo-cd#26897): 3000 Application objects in an
Argo CD informer cache; gzip compression at rest cut memory by ~55% with
only 0.2–0.4 additional CPU cores.  The same problem affects any operator
managing CRDs at scale: Flux, kube-state-metrics, custom controllers.

Measured baseline in this repo: 3000 Pod-sized *unstructured.Unstructured
objects held live in a ThreadSafeStore → ~17.8 MB heap.

Solution
--------
Automatically encode *unstructured.Unstructured objects as CBOR binary blobs
at rest inside the backing map.  No configuration, no opt-in, no API change.
Non-unstructured objects (typed structs, strings, etc.) pass through
unchanged, preserving full backwards compatibility for every existing caller.

Implementation
--------------
thread_safe_store_cbor.go (new file):

  cborEncoded{data []byte}
    Named wrapper type for the at-rest form.  Using a named type rather than
    raw []byte prevents ambiguity: any []byte a caller stores passes through
    unchanged; only values produced by cborEncodeObj carry this wrapper.

  cborDecMode
    Package-level CBOR DecMode configured with
    DefaultMapType=map[string]interface{}.  Without this option fxamacker/cbor
    decodes maps inside interface{} values as map[interface{}]interface{},
    which silently breaks unstructured field accessors such as GetName().

  cborEncodeObj(key, obj)
    Encodes *unstructured.Unstructured to a cborEncoded blob.  Returns obj
    unchanged for any other type.  On encode failure logs a warning and
    returns the original object — codec errors degrade memory savings, not
    correctness.

  cborDecodeObj(key, stored)
    Decodes a cborEncoded blob back to *unstructured.Unstructured.  Returns
    stored unchanged for any other type.  On decode failure logs and returns
    the stored value as-is.

Both helpers are wired into every path that reads from or writes to items:
updateLocked, deleteLocked, Get, List, Index, ByIndex, Replace, AddIndexers.
Indexers always receive the decoded object, never the at-rest blob.

Why CBOR
--------
Four formats were benchmarked (3000 Pod-sized *unstructured.Unstructured,
store holds the only reference, source objects not retained by caller):

  Format          payload/obj   live heap   heap saved   decode ns   list-1k ms
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  identity        ~1603 B       17,758 KB   baseline     4 ns        0.0 ms
  json (no gzip)   1603 B        5,318 KB   -70%         43 µs       31.4 ms
  msgpack          1430 B        6,070 KB   -65%         15 µs       15.4 ms
  cbor             1432 B        4,560 KB   -74%         18 µs       21.7 ms
  json+gzip         507 B        1,567 KB   -91%         71 µs       88.1 ms

CBOR was chosen over the alternatives for these reasons:

  vs json+gzip  — gzip achieves 91% heap reduction vs CBOR's 74%, but its
    read latency (71 µs/obj) and list cost (88 ms / 1000 objects) are 4–6x
    higher than CBOR.  Controllers that resync or list their cache frequently
    (reconcile loops, reflector resyncs) would pay that cost on every cycle.
    The extra 17 percentage points of memory savings is not worth a 4x
    slowdown on the read path for general-purpose use.

  vs msgpack    — msgpack is marginally faster than CBOR (~15 µs vs 18 µs
    decode) but saves less heap (65% vs 74%) and is not vendored in the
    kubernetes repo.  Adding a new external dependency for a 3 µs/object
    latency difference is not justified.

  vs json (no compression) — 3 µs faster to decode than CBOR but saves 4%
    less heap.  No reason to prefer it.

  vs identity   — baseline; included for reference.

CBOR is already a first-class wire format in the Kubernetes API server
(added in 1.32 via fxamacker/cbor/v2) and is a declared dependency of
client-go.  No new dependency is introduced.

Benchmark results (this PR)
---------------------------
  TestCBORHeapReduction  — 3000 Pods, store holds only reference:
    live heap before : ~17,766 KB
    live heap after  :  ~4,741 KB  (~73% reduction)

  BenchmarkCBORWrite :  ~9,600 ns/op   ~200 allocs/op
  BenchmarkCBORRead  : ~17,000 ns/op   ~200 allocs/op
  BenchmarkCBORList  :     ~22 ms / 1000 objects
